role: The whole Watch UI: a vertical-paged TabView (Start / Live metrics / Pause-Stop) that becomes a CompletionScreen after a workout ends, plus sport and zone pickers.
types: SportPickerView, ZonePickerView: struct (private View) — full-screen list pickers
PickerRow: struct (private View) — row with checkmark
PauseStopScreen: struct (private View) — Pause/Resume and End
state: mem:sportOptions (global let: run, walk, bike, treadmill, indoor_bike)
toplevel: Global lets sportOptions and zoneOptions (94-122) are built with String(localized:) at first use. The Start screen offers only 5 of the 10 iPhone sports.

units.does: Root body: CompletionScreen when justCompleted, else the three-page vertical TabView; follows isRecording changes to move between pages.

branches.effect: true: completion view; false: pages with .verticalPage

units.does: NavigationStack wrapping CompletionScreen.
TabView bound to page: StartScreen (in NavigationStack, tag start), LiveMetricsScreen (live), PauseStopScreen (pauseStop).
On recording start jumps from the Start page to Live; on recording end returns from Live or Pause/Stop to Start.
Identity of a sport option = its raw value.
Identity of a zone option = its value.
Short row value: the label ("No target") for 0, else "Zone N".
ScrollView of the Start screen content rows.
Start screen rows in order: reachability banner, title, sport row, target row, Start button, divider, strap pairing row, voice-chat button, status text.
Shows sessionManager.statusLine in caption2 without a line limit.
NavigationLink to SportPickerView bound to selectedSport, labelled with the current sport.
NavigationLink to ZonePickerView bound to selectedZone, labelled with its shortLabel.
Row label: titled icon on the left, value on the right.

Start button: tinted green when the effective strap is connected else orange, disabled while the iPhone is unreachable or a start is in flight, with an accessibility hint describing the strap situation.
Start tap: requests a workout start for the selected sport and zone (nil for 0), then plays the start haptic.

branches.effect: true: targetZone nil (omitted); false: zone value

units.does: Start button label: spinner and "Starting…" while a start is in flight, else play icon and "Start".
Strap pairing NavigationLink (to WatchStrapPairingView), shown in legacy mode or whenever a strap is saved on the Watch.

flags.text: hasSavedStrap is a computed read of UserDefaults, not published state, so the row's visibility only refreshes when some observed property re-renders StartScreen.
USERS_MANUAL says pair from Watch app -> Strap -> Scan, but the pairing row is hidden in display-only mode (the default) unless a strap is already saved, so a new user has no pairing entry.

units.does: Pairing row label: antenna icon plus directStrapButtonLabel.
Talk-to-AI button tinted by voice state and disabled while unreachable or a voice request is in flight.
Talk tap: requests the iPhone voice-chat toggle and plays a click haptic.
Talk button label: spinner while in flight else the state icon, plus voiceChatLabel.
Talk button text: "Starting…" while in flight, else a word for the iPhone voice state, default "Talk to AI".
SF Symbol for the voice state.
Tint for the voice state.
Pairing row text from WatchStrapConnector.connectionState.
True when the Watch's own connector is .connected.

flags.text: Comment says ConnectionState carries associated values "so == won't compile"; WatchStrapConnector.ConnectionState is declared Equatable, so the stated reason for this helper is false.

units.does: Effective strap-connected flag: iPhone's mirrored phoneStrapConnected in display-only mode, the Watch connector's state in legacy mode.
Accessibility hint for Start describing whether a strap (Watch-paired or iPhone-owned) will supply HR.

branches.effect: false: legacy hint branch; true: continue
true: "Strap paired to Watch — tap to start"; false: wrist-sensor warning
false: "iPhone has no strap connected…"; true: continue

units.does: Pairing row tint by connector state.
Ready row when reachable, otherwise the unreachable banner.
Green iPhone icon with "iPhone ready".
Orange banner: "iPhone not reachable" with advice to wake the iPhone and open Emuqu once.
List of sportOptions; tapping one sets the binding and dismisses.
Label with a green checkmark when selected.
List of zoneOptions; tapping one sets the binding and dismisses.

flags.text: Zone labels name Zone 5 "VO₂ max" (and zones 1-4 Recovery/Aerobic/Tempo/Threshold), which the iOS HRZone deliberately avoids: "Zone 5 ≠ VO₂ Max zone until the user provides lab-tested calibration ... without the app over-claiming".

units.does: Live page: metrics while recording, else the connection-status view.
Metrics grid dimmed to 40% with a paused banner while paused, plus the workout-start error note at the bottom.
Orange note with WatchWorkoutManager.lastStartError when the Watch workout session failed to start.
Yellow banner reading "Auto-paused" or "Paused".
Stacks topBar, HR row, divider, pace/time, α1/distance and elevation rows.
Big HR number (displayedHeartRate, locale digits, 44 pt scaled, coloured by hrColor) with "bpm" and the sub-label.

flags.text: The big number can be the direct-strap bpm (displayedHeartRate) while its colour and "% max" sub-label come from the iPhone-relayed hrPercentOfMax of a different source and time, so the colour/percent can disagree with the number shown.

units.does: "N% max" when percent-of-max exists, else "peak N" when peak > 0, else nothing.
Pace cell (paceDisplay or "—") and Time cell (formattedElapsed).
Band-labelled α1 cell and distance cell.
Elevation cell, then cadence when present, else target zone when set, else nothing.

branches.effect: true: "Z<n>" Target cell; false: no right cell

units.does: Sport label and a green/orange reachability dot with matching accessibility label.
HR colour by percent of max: blue <60, green 60-69, yellow 70-79, orange 80-89, red ≥90; primary when unknown.

flags.text: Re-implements the iOS HRZone.classify %-of-max buckets; diverges below 50%: iOS returns no zone (neutral colour) while the Watch colours it blue as zone 1.

units.does: Two-line cell: caption label over monospaced value, given alignment.
Not-recording view: reachability icon and title, current statusLine, and a hint.
"Waiting for workout" when reachable, else "iPhone not reachable".
Hint to swipe to the Start page when reachable, else to open Emuqu on iPhone.

branches.effect: true: swipe hint; false: open-iPhone hint

units.does: Pause/Stop page: header, Resume when paused else Pause, divider, End, status line.

flags.text: The page is always present (WatchLiveView.swift:30-36) and its Pause and End buttons are not gated on isRecording, so with no workout they still send pause/stop requests; with the iPhone unreachable an End is queued for 60 s and blocks other queued taps.

units.does: Pause or play icon (yellow/green) with headerTitle.
"Recording" when not paused, else "Auto-paused" or "Paused".
Resume button: requests resume and plays the start haptic.
Pause button: requests pause and plays a click.
End button: captures reachability, requests stop, ends the Watch's own session immediately when the iPhone was unreachable, plays the stop haptic.
Full-width icon + title button label.
Completion page: saved header, Save & Done button, status line.
Checkmark seal, "Workout saved" and "Your workout is archived on the iPhone…" text.

flags.text: Claims the workout is saved/archived as soon as isRecording flips false, but the iPhone sends that stop from tearDownLiveWorkoutServices before it gathers RR data, finalizes and archives (WorkoutRecorder+Stop.swift:56 vs 59-65); if finalize/archive fails or the phone app is killed in between, the Watch has told the user it is saved.

units.does: Save & Done button: acknowledges the finished workout to the iPhone (clearing justCompleted) and plays the success haptic.
